content:
Let \(\theta=360^\circ/n\). If two sides are separated by \(k\) side-steps, their supporting lines differ in direction by \(k\theta\). To meet at a \(28^\circ\) angle, we need
\[
k\theta \equiv \pm 28^\circ \pmod{180^\circ}.
\]
Since \(0<k\theta<360^\circ\), possible values are
\[
k\theta \in \{28^\circ,152^\circ,208^\circ,332^\circ\}.
\]
Thus \(k/n = r/360\) for \(r\in\{28,152,208,332\}\). For each \(r\), the smallest possible \(n\) is
\[
n=\frac{360}{\gcd(360,r)}.
\]
Computing:
\[
\begin{aligned}
r=28 &: \gcd(360,28)=4 \Rightarrow n=90,\\
r=152 &: \gcd(360,152)=8 \Rightarrow n=45,\\
r=208 &: \gcd(360,208)=8 \Rightarrow n=45,\\
r=332 &: \gcd(360,332)=4 \Rightarrow n=90.
\end{aligned}
\]
The smallest is \(45\). Check: for \(n=45\), \(\theta=8^\circ\), and \(19\theta=152^\circ\), whose supplement is \(28^\circ\).

\[
\boxed{45}
\]
